title: Retention Probability Calculator — v1
content:
Purpose:
This working doc proposes a lightweight, probabilistic customer retention score (0–100 mapped to a retention probability) for use in QBRs, renewal forecasting, and playbook prioritization. The goal is to replace ad-hoc heuristics with a repeatable, interpretable worksheet that CS managers can use in weekly reviews and in renewal prep.

Context / constraints (notes to self):
- Keep model simple: linear weighted signals with a logistic "squash" into a 0–100 probability. Easy to explain to execs.
- Signals available from platform + CS research: usage (tokens/sec, calls/day), feature adoption (embeddings vs completion), latency/quality regressions, support volume, NPS/CSAT, contract dollar, time-to-first-value (TTFV), renewal window.
- Must be calculable from metrics we already collect; avoid requiring heavy new instrumentation.
- Provide clear thresholds for risk flags and playbook actions.

High-level approach:
1) Identify signal buckets and example metrics.
2) Normalize each metric to a 0–1 scale using min/max or percentile mapping.
3) Apply weights to produce a raw health score (0–1).
4) Map raw score through logistic curve to produce retention probability (0–100).
5) Define bands and playbook actions.

Signal definitions (proposed):
- Usage Intensity (weight 0.25): normalized active API calls per day (30d avg). Heavy usage -> higher score.
- Core Feature Penetration (weight 0.20): % of routes using embeddings or advanced features (ratio of distinct product routes using embeddings / total routes).
- Latency & Error Stability (weight 0.15): composite of p95 latency and error rate trends (we invert these so lower latency/err -> higher score).
- Support Friction (weight 0.12): normalized escalations / critical tickets in last 90d (fewer -> higher score).
- Product Sentiment (weight 0.12): last NPS or CSAT normalized to 0–1 (if not available, use customer qualitative signals).
- Contract & Commercial (weight 0.08): % of committed spend utilized + payment status (on time = higher).
- Time-to-Value Recency (weight 0.08): how recent was the last meaningful milestone (integration, first production call) — more recent = higher.

Normalization notes:
- For continuous signals, use percentile clipping: value_normalized = (value - p5) / (p95 - p5) clipped to [0,1]. This reduces influence of outliers.
- For ratio signals (penetration), use direct [0,1] clamp.
- For small-N signals (NPS missing), fallback: qualitative flag mapping {positive:0.75, neutral:0.5, negative:0.25}.

Raw health score (H_raw) calculation (example):
H_raw = sum_i (w_i * signal_i_normalized)
where weights sum to 1.0 (convention above). H_raw in [0,1].

Mapping to retention probability (P_retention):
We want more separation near 0.3–0.7 raw scores. Use a logistic transform:
P_ret = 1 / (1 + exp(-k * (H_raw - x0)))
Parameters: x0 = 0.55 (midpoint tuned to baseline retention), k = 8 (steepness).
Then map to 0–100: P_ret_pct = round(P_ret * 100).
Notes: calibrate k/x0 using historical renewals (see linked JIRA). For initial use, use the parameters above and revise after 90d.

Risk flags (binary triggers to highlight in QBR):
- Rapid usage drop: 30d usage down > 40% vs prior 90d baseline -> FLAG_USAGE_DROP
- Feature stagnation: core feature penetration < 10% after 90d -> FLAG_NO_ADOPTION
- Escalation cluster: >3 Sev1/2 in 90d -> FLAG_ESCALATION
- Payment issues: late payment or churned seat -> FLAG_COMMERCIAL
- Quality regressions: two consecutive deploy-related quality regressions -> FLAG_REGRESSION
- Contract approaching: renewal window <= 90d with H_raw < 0.5 -> FLAG_HIGH_RISK_RENEWAL

Sample worksheet (AcmeCo) — numbers are mock and for walkthrough only:
- Usage intensity (30d avg calls/day): 1,250 -> percentile -> 0.68 (norm) -> contrib = 0.25*0.68 = 0.17
- Core feature penetration: 0.34 -> contrib = 0.20*0.34 = 0.068
- Latency & error stability: normalized = 0.55 -> contrib = 0.15*0.55 = 0.0825
- Support friction: normalized = 0.9 -> contrib = 0.12*0.9 = 0.108
- Product sentiment (CSAT): 0.6 -> contrib = 0.12*0.6 = 0.072
- Contract & commercial: 0.85 -> contrib = 0.08*0.85 = 0.068
- TTFV recency: 0.7 -> contrib = 0.08*0.7 = 0.056
H_raw = sum = 0.6245
Plug into logistic (k=8, x0=0.55): P_ret = 1/(1+exp(-8*(0.6245-0.55))) ≈ 0.64 -> P_ret_pct ≈ 64%
Interpretation: medium risk; recommend targeted engagement.

Band thresholds and suggested playbooks (quick reference):
- Green (P_ret_pct >= 80): "Advocates" — prioritize expansion plays, collect case studies. QBR agenda: usage highlights, upcoming roadmap items, minimal health ops.
- Amber (60–79): "Nudge & Stabilize" — mix of technical enablement and targeted CS touches. QBR agenda: deep dive on top usage drop signals, propose pilot to increase feature adoption, schedule SRE touchpoint if latency flagged.
- Red (<60): "Immediate Risk" — escalate to AE + Solutions Eng, prepare renewal negotiation, remediation plan. QBR agenda: executive summary, remediation milestones (14/30/60d), discount risk modeling.

Action playbook examples (for Red/FLAG_USAGE_DROP):
1) Triage carrier: CS owner opens a 30–60 minute workshop with customer to review recent changes in usage patterns, identify blockers.
2) Technical deep-dive: schedule Solutions Eng session to review integration telemetry and recommend quick fixes (cache sizing, batching, model variant).
3) Outreach cadence: increase touchpoints to weekly until usage recovers; add AE to check commercial signals.
4) Escalation if no improvement in 14d: prepare renewal contingency (discount or migration support budget).

Metrics to track post-playbook:
- 7d and 30d delta in Usage Intensity
- Feature penetration change over 30d
- Ticket volume trend and mean time to resolution (MTTR)
- Customer qualitative score (post-workshop NPS)

Open questions / follow-ups (to prioritize in backlog):
- Need a mapping from SDK-level telemetry to "feature penetration" (work with infra team ticket INFRA-391).
- How to treat free-tier customers vs committed spend in contract weight? (propose separate baseline for free/Pilot).
- Calibration: pull historical renewal outcomes for last 18 months to fit logistic params (JIRA: CS-forecast-calibrate).
- Alerting: implement automated flag generation in CS dashboard and route to #cs-triage Slack.

Notes on explainability for QBRs:
- Keep the math visible: show the normalized inputs and contribution bars. Managers like to see where the score came from.
- For execs, show P_ret_pct + 2–3 bullet drivers and proposed owner for each remediation.

Quick implementation checklist (MVP):
- [ ] Add normalized fields to CS dashboard (product metrics team)
- [ ] Build a spreadsheet template for CS managers (this doc -> sheet)
- [ ] Create auto-flagging rules and Slack hooks (ENG-ops)
- [ ] Run 90d pilot with 15 renewal accounts, refine weights and logistic params

Appendix: short examples of normalization functions (implementation notes):
- percentile_clip(value, p5, p95) = max(0, min(1, (value - p5) / (p95 - p5)))
- invert_error_metric(err_rate) = 1 - percentile_clip(err_rate, p5_err, p95_err) // so lower err = higher health

Owner notes: this is intentionally pragmatic and conservative. Aim for adoption first; accuracy improvements come after we collect labeled renewal outcomes. Use the pilot to validate whether weights need rebalancing (usage vs commercial often fight).

Related artifacts and history:
- See `customer-signal-index-builder.json` and `risk-flag-triage-matrix.json` in this folder for previous heuristics. This doc reframes as a probability and ties thresholds to QBR playbooks.

Next steps for me (Aisha):
- Share with Priya + Ethan for review by 2025-09-07.
- Kick off a spreadsheet template and link it into CS playbook Confluence page.
- Draft a short training triage play for CS managers (15–30 minute session).

End of working draft v1.
